📚 Today you learned

Segment-Level Halal Screening (Diversified Conglomerates)

A company can pass the halal test at the headline level and still fail it underneath. SPXC's top-line business is HVAC and cooling technology — clean. But its Detection & Measurement segment includes Kranze Technology Solutions, a $340M defense-electronics subsidiary building for the US military — and that single segment is why the whole position trips your no-defense-contractor rule, even though it's a rounding error against SPXC's total revenue. The lesson: "what does this company do" isn't answered by the ticker's primary sector tag, it's answered by reading the segment breakdown in the 10-K. A conglomerate's ugliest segment decides the halal call, not its biggest one.

Also today: 10-K Item 1 — the "Business" section of the annual report where segment-level revenue and descriptions actually live; that's where you'd catch a Kranze before entry, not after.
